lesson: Gate commits behind one script that exits non-zero, with set -e. A heredoc's failing exit status does not chain into the next line; two pushes went out on failed tests before this was fixed.
Never put backticks in a git -m string — bash command-substitutes them and the word vanishes from the message.
Verify a data migration on a SEEDED database with bound parameters. A ':100' inside a JSON literal in sa.text() is a bind parameter; the insert failed and the migration 'passed' on an empty table.

A balance-sheet tie-out inside one self-consistent model ties straight through a sign error. Catch sign errors with direction tests (a -95k draw must reduce cash by 95k) and the reference workbook — not with another identity.
Grading actual/target by ratio is wrong whenever the target is negative (two negatives compare magnitudes). Grade the difference in the favourable direction over |target|, in integer arithmetic.

A number is input or derived in ONE place and carried everywhere. Two copies of a formula (JS for display, stored copy for grading) guarantee drift; prove a port key-for-key before deleting the original.
create_all before Alembic creates tables the ledger doesn't know about and never alters existing ones. Migrate first on every launch; make migrations idempotent.
Don't cherry-pick files across diverged branches — it silently drops the other side's work on shared files. Merge first, then build.
When one upload shape is wrong (two Balance Sheets, no P&L) the screen looks plausible. Say it — a warning beats a screen the user has to notice is sparse.
